cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Apologize for the Lie
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that the concealment or misdirection mattered, even if the underlying choice was defensible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I'm not asking you to apologise for cancelling. Apologise for not telling me. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't want to upset you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. So you let me arrive with a cake instead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry the party didn't happen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try the part where I didn't know.

mechanism: A manages a conversation over the unused party cake and offers a cooperative setting while demanding acknowledgment of nondisclosure rather than cancellation.
confusable: Unlike wanting the party restored, A accepts the underlying choice and focuses on being left uninformed; authority makes room for B while directing the apology.
comparison: A cancelled social event and protective excuse differ from an ongoing adoption and proposed financial repair.
seedUse: D123-a unannounced cancellation and cake arrival; S02-b uses a concrete shared activity to keep B engaged while narrowing the demand.
